newsitem.title: USA: Deal offered to protect Alaska's Kenai Fjords park.
newsitem.headline: Deal offered to protect Alaska's Kenai Fjords park.

text.p: Federal and state officials offered Friday to spend some Exxon Valdez oil spill settlement money to shelter from development 32,500 acres of park and wildlife refuge.

The Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council made its $15.2 million offer to the English Bay Corp., an Alaska Native village group with ownership rights to key coastal parcels in the popular Kenai Fjords National Park and the adjacent Alaska Maritime National Willdife Refuge.

The offer capped four years of negotiations between English Bay's Alutiiq owners and the trustee council, which manages the $900 million that Exxon has promised to pay to settle government civil claims over the nation's worst oil spill.

The deal includes $14.1 million from the civil settlement for acquisition of the land parcels, plus $1.1 million in criminal settlement funds to compensate for relinquished native hunting rights, officials said.

Most of the property involved in the transaction is along the coastline of the scenic 580,000-acre national park, one of Alaska's top tourist destinations. About 2,270 acres is within the wildlife refuge.
Kenai Fjords, a wildlife haven at the tip of Alaska's Kenai Peninsula, was marred by oil that drifted west from Prince William Sound in the 1989 disaster.
